title: Karna turns down a throne
hookLine: the peace talks are over, and Krishna invites Karna up into his chariot for a ride outside the city.
carry: keeping faith is dharma, even when it costs a crown
tomorrow: what does Karna give the mother who gave him away?

cards: A chariot rolls out through the gates of Hastinapura. The embassy has failed. Duryodhana won't give the Pandavas their share, and war is coming.
But before Krishna goes, he does something odd. He calls Karna, Duryodhana's friend and champion, up beside him, and the two ride out of the city together, away from the crowd.
What Krishna says on that ride could stop the war before it starts, and it rests on a secret about who Karna's mother is.

teach.b: Here is the secret. Karna is Kunti's son, born to her before she married Pandu. That makes him, Krishna says, the eldest brother of the five Pandavas.

teach.h: THE OFFER: BROTHERS AND A THRONE
teach.b: Then comes the offer. Come with me. Your brothers will touch your feet.
You will be king, and Yudhishthira himself will stand behind your throne. Karna's answer is the heart of today. He says he already knows.
Then he says why it changes nothing. His mother set him adrift as a newborn.

teach.h: RADHA RAISED ME; I STAY HER SON
teach.b: A charioteer named Adhiratha found him, and Adhiratha's wife Radha raised him. Her milk fed him and her love kept him alive, he says, and he will not stop being her son for a crown.
He married among the charioteer's people, and he has children there. And for years Duryodhana has stood by him when no one else would. He gave Duryodhana his word, and he means to keep it.
Then he asks Krishna for one thing: don't tell Yudhishthira. If Yudhishthira learned that Karna was his elder brother, he would hand him the kingdom, and Karna would hand it straight to Duryodhana.

teach.h: HE KEEPS FAITH, AND PAYS FOR IT
teach.b: Better that it stays secret. So a man is offered everything he ever wanted, and turns it down for the people who loved him first.
In Hindu teaching, gratitude, remembering who held you up, is part of dharma, and so is keeping your word. Karna holds to both. But he holds them on Duryodhana's side, and that's the knot.
Many teachers say Karna is right by one duty and ruinous by another, and the epic honors him and grieves him at once.

how: Krishna's conversation with Karna is read as part of the Udyoga book of the Mahabharata, and Karna's choice to stay with the family who raised him is retold in story, song and performance.

o: the getting ready: the book where each side makes its choices
the long years of exile the Pandavas spent in the forest
the fighting itself, once the two armies meet on the field

games.q: who's who on the ride? tap the pairs.

s: Karna was shocked to learn who his mother was
he tells Krishna he already knows.
Krishna offered Karna the throne if he joined the Pandavas
Krishna says his brothers would honor him and he would be king.
the epic treats Karna's loyalty as simply wrong
it honors his gratitude and his kept word, and grieves where they lead him.

games.q: you're Karna. Krishna offers you brothers, honor and a throne. your friend Duryodhana is about to go to war. what do you say?
o: no: I stay with those who raised me and stood by me.
I'll stay out of the war entirely.
games.why: Karna refuses. he names Radha, who raised him, and Duryodhana, who stood by him: gratitude and his word come first. then he asks Krishna to keep the secret.

practice: Bring to mind someone who raised you, or stood by you when no one else did. Many Hindus honor that by touching the feet of parents and elders, a pranam.
Breathing in, picture their face; breathing out, bow to them in your mind, or for real the next time you see them. If you don't pray, just thank them, silently or out loud.

wordCard.voice: Udyoga. The preparing, the getting ready for war: the book where every side makes its choices before the fighting begins. Today, Karna made his.

orig.note: the name of the Mahabharata's fifth book, the Udyoga Parva, the book of getting ready for war.
